text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: High error rates for private/on-prem customers in Azure francecentral (egress DNS failures observed) — auto-escalation to SRE oncall. Alerts: 503s + connection timeouts on private endpoints.

sre-oncall-maya: seeing spike in 503s for routes that use our FRANCECENTRAL egress. Dashboard: per-token latency up, KV cache pressure small. Marking P1 for availability.

alex_prodeng: which customers impacted? any Dedicated clusters on private peering?

sre-oncall-maya: initial list from telemetry: 6 customers with Dedicated + Private vnet peering, 2 with on-prem VPNs. Sample errors: TLS handshakes failing, dig to internal private DNS times out.

elaine_cs: reaching out to affected customer CSMs with initial note: "we're investigating networking egress issue in francecentral affecting private connectivity; operations team engaged, will update in 15"

sam_network: running quick checks from our egress routers. Observed intermittent DNS resolution failures to private zones, NXDOMAIN then timeout. Pairing with cloud provider -- raising ticket.

netops: looks like BGP route flap on a pair of FRANCECENTRAL egress peering devices — some paths are asymmetrically routing to a noisy edge causing packet loss to our private peering.

sre-oncall-maya: temporary mitigation plan: 1) pin affected traffic to alternate region (westeurope) via policy routing for affected customers, 2) force local DNS fallback to cached entries for 60s, 3) enable faster KV cache warmup to avoid regen.

alex_prodeng: can we programmatically re-route just the impacted peering sessions? need to avoid global customer churn.

sam_network: yes, we can push a routing policy that prefers westeurope for those specific prefixes and tag with route-map quick-failover-1745. Doing a dry-run now.

deploy-bot: Started job job-apply-route-1745 (id: run-7821). Steps: plan -> apply.

sre-oncall-maya: applying route-map now. Expect 30s for route propagation, will monitor.

netops: cloud provider confirmed unusual maintenance on an aggregation switch, they claim a partial roll-back in progress. Still seeing DNS queries hit unhealthy edge.

sre-oncall-maya: after apply: error rate dropped ~70% for the flagged customers. Instrumentation: per-route 95p latency back to normal. Continuing to watch for flapping.

elaine_cs: updated customers: "We've applied a temporary network reroute to mitigate the issue and are monitoring. We'll follow up after provider completes maintenance."

alex_prodeng: can we keep this mitigation for the full maintenance window? any cost or perf tradeoffs we should call out?

sam_network: tradeoff: slightly higher latency (~25ms) for rerouted traffic but avoids failures. cost impact minimal for now.

sre-oncall-maya: handoff: I've stabilized traffic and will keep the rotation for the next 2 hours while netops and provider finish repairs. Handoff to night SRE (netops) in 20m. Tagging for postmortem and RCA.

netops: acknowledged, will monitor overnight and collect pcap/flow logs for the window.

alex_prodeng: good job. When stable, we should add an automated policy to detect egress DNS path degradation and failover automatically. Filing follow-up ticket.

incident-bot: Incident updated: status -> mitigated (partial). Next update due in 30 minutes or on any regression. :eyes:

elaine_cs: starting templated customer follow-up for impacted list now.

sre-oncall-maya: leaving notes: mitigation applied (route-map quick-failover-1745), affected prefixes listed in the runbook, actions for postmortem: collect traceroutes, BGP RIB snapshots, provider comms.

alex_prodeng: assign postmortem owner? I'll take it with netops.

netops: I'll gather logs and timeline from provider.

incident-bot: Paging summary: root cause suspected: provider edge device instability causing DNS egress packet loss -> partial mitigation via regional route preference to westeurope. Next: RCA and customer comms.
